# `.well-known/*` endpoint audit — help.qrtub.com

**Fetched:** 2026-08-19, via `curl -s` (body) and `curl -sI` (headers) against the live site.
**Method reference:** `/workspace/mintlify-docs/audit/_raw/mintlify-guidance.md` (read first — it establishes what Mintlify's own docs say triggers/configures each endpoint family, so this file only adds the *live* observations and the accuracy cross-check).

All four endpoints are confirmed live and auto-generated by Mintlify with zero explicit configuration in this repo's `docs.json` — but two of the four carry a naming artifact that traces directly to a `docs.json` field, and one is overridable from this repo if desired. Details below.

---

## 1. `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`

**Status:** `HTTP/2 200`
**Content-Type:** `application/json`
**Cache-Control:** `public, max-age=86400`
**Other headers:** `access-control-allow-origin: *`, `x-matched-path: /_mintlify/mcp/[subdomain]/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`, served via Vercel.

### Full raw body

```json
{"name":"QRtub documentation Docs MCP","description":"Search and retrieve QRtub documentation documentation","version":"1.0.0","serverInfo":{"name":"QRtub documentation Docs MCP","version":"1.0.0"},"url":"https://help.qrtub.com/mcp","transport":"http","capabilities":{"tools":true,"resources":true},"authentication":"none","tools":[{"name":"search_q_rtub_documentation","description":"Search across the QRtub documentation knowledge base to find relevant information, code examples, API references, and guides. Use this tool when you need to answer questions about QRtub documentation, find specific documentation, understand how features work, or locate implementation details. The search returns contextual content with titles and direct links to the documentation pages. If you need the full content of a specific page, use the query_docs_filesystem tool to `head` or `cat` the page path (append `.mdx` to the path returned from search — e.g. `head -200 /api-reference/create-customer.mdx`).","inputSchema":{"type":"object","properties":{"query":{"type":"string","description":"A query to search the content with."}},"required":["query"]},"annotations":{"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}},{"name":"query_docs_filesystem_q_rtub_documentation","description":"Run a read-only shell-like query against a virtualized, in-memory filesystem rooted at `/` that contains ONLY the QRtub documentation documentation pages and OpenAPI specs. This is NOT a shell on any real machine — nothing runs on the user's computer, the server host, or any network. The filesystem is a sandbox backed by documentation chunks.\n\nThis is how you read documentation pages: there is no separate \"get page\" tool. To read a page, pass its `.mdx` path (e.g. `/quickstart.mdx`, `/api-reference/create-customer.mdx`) to `head` or `cat`. To search the docs with exact keyword or regex matches, use `rg`. To understand the docs structure, use `tree` or `ls`.\n\n**Workflow:** Start with the search tool for broad or conceptual queries like \"how to authenticate\" or \"rate limiting\". Use this tool when you need exact keyword/regex matching, structural exploration, or to read the full content of a specific page by path.\n\nSupported commands: rg (ripgrep), grep, find, tree, ls, cat, head, tail, stat, wc, sort, uniq, cut, sed, awk, jq, plus basic text utilities. No writes, no network, no process control. Run `--help` on any command for usage.\n\nEach call is STATELESS: the working directory always resets to `/` and no shell variables, aliases, or history carry over between calls. If you need to operate in a subdirectory, chain commands in one call with `&&` or pass absolute paths (e.g., `cd /api-reference && ls` or `ls /api-reference`). Do NOT assume that `cd` in one call affects the next call.\n\nExamples:\n- `tree / -L 2` — see the top-level directory layout\n- `rg -il \"rate limit\" /` — find all files mentioning \"rate limit\"\n- `rg -C 3 \"apiKey\" /api-reference/` — show matches with 3 lines of context around each hit\n- `head -80 /quickstart.mdx` — read the top 80 lines of a specific page\n- `head -80 /quickstart.mdx /installation.mdx /guides/first-deploy.mdx` — read multiple pages in one call\n- `cat /api-reference/create-customer.mdx` — read a full page when you need everything\n- `cat /openapi/spec.json | jq '.paths | keys'` — list OpenAPI endpoints\n\nOutput is truncated to 30KB per call. Prefer targeted `rg -C` or `head -N` over broad `cat` on large files. To read only the relevant sections of a large file, use `rg -C 3 \"pattern\" /path/file.mdx`. Batch multiple file reads into a single `head` or `cat` call whenever possible.\n\nWhen referencing pages in your response to the user, convert filesystem paths to URL paths by removing the `.mdx` extension. For example, `/quickstart.mdx` becomes `/quickstart` and `/api-reference/overview.mdx` becomes `/api-reference/overview`.","inputSchema":{"type":"object","properties":{"command":{"type":"string","description":"A shell command to run against the virtualized documentation filesystem (e.g., `rg -il \"keyword\" /`, `tree / -L 2`, `head -80 /path/file.mdx`)."}},"required":["command"]},"annotations":{"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}}]}
```

### Assessment

**Confirmed live and functional.** A sanity-check `POST` to `https://help.qrtub.com/mcp` with a proper MCP `initialize` payload but without the required dual `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` header returned:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Not Acceptable: Client must accept both application/json and text/event-stream"},"id":null}
```

That is standard MCP Streamable HTTP transport behavior (per the MCP spec, not a QRtub bug) — it confirms a real MCP server is listening at the advertised `/mcp` URL, it just needs the correct `Accept` header to proceed past `initialize`.

**Naming defect — `"QRtub documentation documentation"`:** Mintlify's own docs (`/docs/ai/model-context-protocol`) give the generic template for this field as `"Search and retrieve your documentation"`, where "your documentation" is filled in from the project's configured name. QRtub's `docs.json` sets the required top-level `name` field to `"QRtub documentation"` (see `/workspace/mintlify-docs/docs.json` line 4). Mintlify's template appends the literal word "documentation" to that name, producing the doubled `"Search and retrieve QRtub documentation documentation"` — and the same pattern doubles into `serverInfo.name`: `"QRtub documentation Docs MCP"`.

**This is configurable from this repo.** `docs.json`'s `name` field is documented (`/workspace/mintlify-docs/audit/_raw/raw_organize_settings-reference.md` line 111) as "The name of your project, organization, or product" — a required string with no other purpose called out beyond that. Changing it from `"QRtub documentation"` to `"QRtub"` would almost certainly collapse the doubling into `"Search and retrieve QRtub documentation"` and `"QRtub Docs MCP"`. The trade-off: this same field also drives the site's browser-tab title and any other place Mintlify surfaces the project name, so changing it is a site-wide naming decision, not a narrowly-scoped fix — flag for a human decision rather than changing unilaterally.

**Tool descriptions are accurate and generic** — they describe Mintlify's own standard search/filesystem tools, not QRtub-specific claims, so there is nothing here to fact-check against QRtub's product.

## 2. `/.well-known/agent-card.json`

**Status:** `HTTP/2 200`
**Content-Type:** `application/json`
**Cache-Control:** `public, max-age=86400`
**Other headers:** `content-security-policy: worker-src * blob: data: 'unsafe-eval' 'unsafe-inline'; object-src data: ; base-uri 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests; frame-ancestors 'self' https://dashboard.mintlify.com https://app.mintlify.com; form-action 'self' https://codesandbox.io`, `x-matched-path: /_sites/[subdomain]/.well-known/agent-card.json`, served via Vercel.

### Full raw body

```json
{"name":"QRtub documentation","url":"https://help.qrtub.com/","version":"1.0.0","protocolVersion":"0.3","preferredTransport":"HTTP+JSON","supportedInterfaces":[{"url":"https://help.qrtub.com/","protocolBinding":"HTTP+JSON","protocolVersion":"0.3"}],"provider":{"url":"https://help.qrtub.com/","organization":"QRtub documentation"},"documentationUrl":"https://help.qrtub.com/","capabilities":{"streaming":false,"pushNotifications":false},"defaultInputModes":["text/plain"],"defaultOutputModes":["text/plain"],"skills":[{"id":"teralis","name":"Teralis","description":"Use when managing QR code deployments at scale, connecting physical items to digital systems, setting up print-first workflows, configuring multi-destination landing pages, integrating with inspection and maintenance platforms, or routing users based on device type and item data.","tags":[],"url":"https://help.qrtub.com/.well-known/agent-skills/teralis/skill.md"}]}
```

### Assessment

This is Mintlify's A2A (Agent-to-Agent) agent card, auto-generated with no config in `docs.json` (per the guidance file, §3b). Two things stand out:

- **`"name": "QRtub documentation"` and `"provider.organization": "QRtub documentation"`** — both directly echo the `docs.json` top-level `name` field verbatim (no doubling bug here, since the template just uses the raw string). `"QRtub documentation"` as an "organization" name reads a little oddly machine-to-machine (an agent parsing this card would infer the organization is literally named "QRtub documentation"), but it is not inaccurate — it is exactly what's configured. Same fix lever as finding 1: changing `docs.json.name` would change this too.
- **The one listed skill is `id: "teralis"`, `name: "Teralis"`, not `"QRtub"`.** This is the more substantive finding — see §3/§4 below, since the same skill is what `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json` and `/.well-known/agent-skills/teralis/skill.md` also serve.

## 3. `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`

**Status:** `HTTP/2 200`
**Content-Type:** `application/json`
**Cache-Control:** `public, max-age=86400`
**Other headers:** same CSP/Vercel signature as agent-card.json above. `x-matched-path: /_sites/[subdomain]/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`.

### Full raw body

```json
{"$schema":"https://schemas.agentskills.io/discovery/0.2.0/schema.json","skills":[{"name":"teralis","type":"skill-md","description":"Use when managing QR code deployments at scale, connecting physical items to digital systems, setting up print-first workflows, configuring multi-destination landing pages, integrating with inspection and maintenance platforms, or routing users based on device type and item data.","url":"/.well-known/agent-skills/teralis/skill.md","digest":"sha256:702cc3bb5cd882a8fad3d157807228787c6431389e36208285da60bec51dfa3c"}]}
```

### Where the `"teralis"` name comes from

Fetching the referenced skill file (`https://help.qrtub.com/.well-known/agent-skills/teralis/skill.md`, 200 OK, `content-type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8`) shows its frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: Teralis
description: Use when managing QR code deployments at scale, connecting physical items to digital systems, setting up print-first workflows, configuring multi-destination landing pages, integrating with inspection and maintenance platforms, or routing users based on device type and item data.
metadata:
    mintlify-proj: teralis
    version: "1.0"
---

# Teralis (QRtub) Skill
```

`metadata.mintlify-proj: teralis` is the tell: this is Mintlify's **internal project slug** (almost certainly set when the Mintlify project/dashboard entry was first created, presumably before the product was branded "QRtub" — `CLAUDE.md` confirms the product is owned by "Teralis Pty Ltd", so "teralis" was plausibly the original project name in Mintlify's dashboard). It is **not sourced from `docs.json`** — nothing in `docs.json` mentions "Teralis" or "teralis"; the top-level `name` field is `"QRtub documentation"`. So this cannot be fixed by editing `docs.json`.

**Is it configurable from this repo?** Yes, but only via override, not via `docs.json`. Per Mintlify's `/docs/ai/skillmd` page (fetched live for this check):

> "Add a custom `skill.md` file to the root of your project to override the automatically generated file."

and, for multiple skills:

> "Add multiple skill files to the `.mintlify/skills/` directory in your project. Each skill must be in its own subdirectory with a `SKILL.md` file... the discovery index includes all skills."

So the fix, if QRtub wants it, is to add a `skill.md` (or `.mintlify/skills/qrtub/SKILL.md`) file to this repo with `name: QRtub` (or similar) in its frontmatter — the auto-generated "teralis"-named one would then be fully superseded (Mintlify: "If you delete all custom skill files, Mintlify generates a new `skill.md` file" — implying the reverse is also true, a custom file suppresses the auto-generated one). This is not something currently present anywhere in `/workspace/mintlify-docs` — grepped for `skill.md` and `.mintlify/skills` in the repo root, no matches.

### Assessment of the skill.md *content itself* (not just the name)

The body of the skill file is otherwise a reasonably accurate summary of QRtub's product mechanics — cross-checked against `CLAUDE.md` and the live docs:

- Entity model (Link/Item/Tub/Page/Destination/Media/Batch), Link types (`qrtub.com/r/x5fgd` random example matches `CLAUDE.md`'s own example verbatim), field-binding syntax (`{{item.fieldName}}`, exact-as-stored insertion, no auto-encoding), and the "unconnected codes don't 404, they show a neutral branded page" gotcha are all consistent with `CLAUDE.md` and the live pages fetched below.
- It correctly avoids overclaiming integration ("routes to" / "opens... pre-filled", never "syncs with" or "writes back"), matching `CLAUDE.md`'s "What integration means here" rule.
- It correctly does **not** claim per-item Media tracking (inventory/material/cost) — consistent with `CLAUDE.md`'s explicit correction that print batches are tracked but individual media is not.

**One real accuracy gap, inherited from the published docs it was generated from, not invented by the skill itself:** the skill.md's "Common Field References" section lists `session.user.id`, `session.user.email`, `session.user.name` as available in URL Templates/conditions, and its "Quick Reference" table omits any `time.*` field. Cross-checking against the live pages:

- `https://help.qrtub.com/help/using-fields.md` and `https://help.qrtub.com/help/conditional-visibility.md` **both independently document a full "Session Fields" section** (`session.user`, `session.user.id`, `session.user.email`, `session.user.name`, with a worked example `session.user != null`) — so the skill.md is faithfully reflecting what's actually published on the site, not fabricating anything on its own.
- **But `CLAUDE.md`'s own "Conditional visibility" section — the file this repo treats as source-of-truth for what's verified against `../qrtub/src/`** — lists only four context namespaces as available in a CEL expression: "Item fields, Tub fields, Device fields, Time fields (`time.hour`, `time.dayOfWeek`, `time.dayOfMonth`, `time.month`, `time.year`, `time.isWeekend`)". It does not mention a `session` namespace at all, and it states plainly: **"There is no current-date value and no date arithmetic."** It further calls out `today` as a specific example of a value that was invented and published without ever existing in the code.
- Neither `help/using-fields.md` nor `help/conditional-visibility.md` (both fetched in full for this check) mentions any `time.*` field anywhere — the entire `time` namespace `CLAUDE.md` says exists is absent from the live docs those pages that the skill.md was auto-generated from.

**Net effect:** the `.well-known` skill.md content is an accurate mirror of what `help.qrtub.com` currently publishes, but what's published disagrees with this repo's own verified source-of-truth file on two specific points — a `session.*` field family that `CLAUDE.md` doesn't list as existing, and a `time.*` field family that `CLAUDE.md` says exists but the live pages never mention. Given `CLAUDE.md`'s explicit warning about exactly this failure mode (features/values documented from assumption rather than the code — `today`, automatic URL encoding, scan history, and per-item Media tracking are the four it names as prior incidents), this `session` vs. `time` discrepancy reads as the same pattern recurring on `help/using-fields.md` and `help/conditional-visibility.md`, and it is now propagating into the AI-agent-facing skill.md precisely because that file is auto-summarized from the (possibly-wrong) page content rather than the app source. This is a docs-content finding, not a `.well-known`-mechanism finding — it belongs to whoever owns `help/using-fields.mdx` and `help/conditional-visibility.mdx`, but it's surfaced here because it's the one substantive place the `.well-known` content's accuracy against "QRtub's actual docs" breaks down. Recommend verifying `session.*` and `time.*` against `../qrtub/src/lib/page/context.ts` directly rather than trusting either the live page or the skill.md.

Everything else in the skill.md (entities, link types, batch lifecycle, gotchas, resource links) checked out against `CLAUDE.md` and/or the live llms.txt-listed pages with no discrepancies found.

## 4. `/.well-known/api-catalog`

**Status:** `HTTP/2 404`
**Content-Type:** `text/plain;charset=UTF-8`
**Cache-Control:** `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`
**Other headers:** same CSP/Vercel signature, `x-matched-path: /_sites/[subdomain]/.well-known/api-catalog`.

### Full raw body

```
Not Found
```

### Assessment

**Genuinely absent, not a fluke or a caching artifact** — the 404 has `must-revalidate, max-age=0`, i.e. Mintlify is not even willing to cache this as a hit, consistent with a route that simply doesn't exist for this deployment. This matches the guidance file's finding (§3c): **no page in Mintlify's published documentation set (`docs.json` reference, SEO reference, MCP page, skill.md page, or API settings page) mentions an `api-catalog` well-known endpoint at all.** `api-catalog` is a real IETF-adjacent convention (RFC 9727 / `api-catalog` well-known URI for API description discovery) but nothing suggests Mintlify implements it. Given QRtub's docs.json has no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec configured (no `api` object in `docs.json`, no `.well-known/api-catalog`-relevant settings anywhere in `settings-api`), there's also no underlying API surface this endpoint would even have content to describe. **Not configurable from this repo** — there is no `docs.json` field or repo-root file convention that produces this path; it would need to appear as an actual Mintlify platform feature (undocumented today) before there'd be anything to turn on.

## Cross-cutting summary

| Endpoint | Status | Auto-generated, zero-config? | Configurable from this repo? | Accuracy vs. real docs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` | 200 | Yes | Indirectly — `docs.json` top-level `name` field feeds the doubled `"...documentation documentation"` string | Tool descriptions accurate/generic; naming has a cosmetic doubling bug traceable to `docs.json.name` |
| `/.well-known/agent-card.json` | 200 | Yes | Indirectly — same `docs.json.name` field feeds `name`/`provider.organization`; skill listed comes from skill.md (see next row) | Accurate mechanically; `provider.organization: "QRtub documentation"` reads oddly but isn't wrong |
| `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json` (+ referenced `teralis/skill.md`) | 200 | Yes | **Yes, directly** — a root `skill.md` or `.mintlify/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in this repo would override the auto-generated "teralis"-named one | Skill content is a faithful summary of the live docs and matches `CLAUDE.md` almost everywhere; inherits a `session.*`/`time.*` field discrepancy from `help/using-fields.mdx` and `help/conditional-visibility.mdx` that contradicts `CLAUDE.md`'s source-of-truth field list |
| `/.well-known/api-catalog` | 404 | N/A — doesn't exist | No — not a documented Mintlify feature, nothing in `docs.json` would produce it | N/A |

**Two concrete, low-risk repo-side actions worth flagging to a human (not made unilaterally here):**
1. Add a custom `skill.md` (or `.mintlify/skills/qrtub/SKILL.md`) at the repo root, naming it "QRtub" instead of inheriting Mintlify's internal "teralis" project slug, and correcting the `session.*`/`time.*` field list once that's verified against `../qrtub/src/lib/page/context.ts`.
2. Consider whether `docs.json`'s top-level `name` should be `"QRtub"` rather than `"QRtub documentation"` — it would fix the `"documentation documentation"` doubling in the MCP server-card, at the cost of also changing the site's browser-tab title and anywhere else Mintlify surfaces the project name site-wide.

Neither of these is `.well-known`-endpoint-specific misconfiguration; both are `docs.json`/repo-content choices that happen to surface through these endpoints.
